proposed_edges.relationship: Latour describes actor-network theory as a change of metaphor from surfaces to filaments, ‘or rhyzomes in Deleuze’s parlance’, and likens a network that has no outside to ‘Deleuze’s lightning rod’ (written 1990; English 1996)
proposed_edges.evidence_note: His own words, read 2026-10-31 in the author's web version (P-67) of ‘On Actor-Network Theory: A Few Clarifications plus More than a Few Complications’ (written 1990; Danish in Philosophia 25:3–4; English in Soziale Welt 47, 1996, pp. 369–381). Web p. 3: ‘Put too simply AT is a change of methaphors to describe essences: instead of surfaces one gets filaments (or rhyzomes in Deleuze’s parlance 197-).’ Web p. 6: a network ‘is not a foreground over a background, nor a crack onto a solid soil, it is like Deleuze’s lightning rod that creates by the same stroke the background and the foreground (Deleuze, 197-)’. Spellings and the unfinished ‘197-’ references are in the draft. Two acknowledged borrowings of image and vocabulary in a programmatic text; not a claim that ANT derives from Deleuze, and printed Soziale Welt pages are not collated. Latour's 1997 Keele talk ‘On Recalling ANT’ (Lancaster web version, read) attributes the label ‘actant-rhyzome ontology’ to Mike Lynch and does not mention Deleuze, so it is not cited for this edge.
